correctness.rationale: A symmetric three-edge-per-petal subdivision meets the two-particle Abrams criterion. Every cubical 2-cell falls into exactly one of two types and admits an explicitly free 1-face; a constructive connectivity argument gives H1 rank 1+3 binom(m,2). Every fixed oriented 0/1/2 cell under any signed permutation is counted with its orientation sign; the Euler–Lefschetz trace 1-t0+t1-t2 simplifies to the claimed character. Uniform group averages yield invariant dimensions 2 and 0 for all m>=2. An independently encoded cubical verifier checks all 4282 signed permutations for m<=5 and the complete finite collapses; finite checks support but do not replace the unrestricted proof. The argument uses no numerical or generalization leap.

originality.rationale: The claim is the complete character of ordinary rational H1 of two UNORDERED points on a rose under signed loop permutations. Closest primary papers cover homological dimension, discretizations, ordered-generator sets, and nonequivariant Betti groups; a different framework studies compactly supported ordered configurations. No inspected stronger theorem or exact table implies the displayed signed character and invariant-drop conclusion without a new fixed-cell calculation. value.rationale: The rose is a canonical one-essential-vertex cyclic graph family; its two-particle graph braid homology records distinct particle motions. A uniform class function for the full signed wreath-product symmetry, valid for every m, strictly refines all nonequivariant rank information. The sharp two-versus-zero invariant-homology contrast is not detectable from Betti numbers and makes precise the effect of allowing petal reversals. The fixed-cell cancellation is structural and extends beyond a single finite calculation or arbitrary numeric increment.
